b: Thank you. I’ve found some incredibly helpful perspectives here. I’m using a throwaway account for obvious reasons. I really need some advice, particularly from men who may have experienced something similar.

About 10 years ago, I discovered my husband looking up women on social media, using pornography and dating apps, and making enquiries about escorts (although I’m 100% certain he never followed through, due concerns about STDs).

He was going through a particularly dark period at the time. His ex had told him she had slept with multiple partners while they were together, and I believe he turned to these behaviours as coping mechanisms and a way of seeking validation, particularly through dating apps. He never actually met anyone.

We eventually worked through it and decided to get married. I would describe myself as happily married. My husband is wonderful in many ways. He loves me, takes care of everything at home and is a good partner. Nobody would suspect we have problems.
However, physical intimacy has always been lacking. We have sex only a few times a year.

Looking back, I think the discoveries 10 years ago affected me more deeply than I realised. Although I forgave him, I never fully processed the betrayal. I developed insecurities around feeling special, desired and sexually vulnerable with him.

I think I gradually built emotional barriers and began rejecting his sexual advances quite frequently. I loved him but struggled to be completely vulnerable during sex (which leads to the inability to orgasm). I was comparing myself and doubting my attractiveness.

We never addressed the bedroom problems. Fast forward 10 years, I tried to initiate sex 4 times in a week and thought it will make my husband a happy man as I’m finally open to surrender and be sexually vulnerable. I don’t know the exact reason but it happened.

Instead of feeling elated, my husband told me that he used to desire me sexually, but after years of rejection, he gradually conditioned himself not to desire me anymore. Eventually, he stopped initiating and says he has almost completely lost his sexual desire for me.

He still loves me, kisses and cuddles me, but says he no longer feels the sexual spark. He said I am a beautiful woman (which I believed I am, have a body that men desires and well endowed), and that I still attracts him, but not sexual desire.

The main issue is that he watches porn and masturbate regularly. He seems more sexually responsive to porn than to intimacy with me. And told me outright he used to prefer sex with me, but now prefer porn over me. During sex, he sometimes loses his erection and struggles to reach orgasm. I believe this is porn-induced erectile dysfunction.
Please let me know if pornography contributed to his loss of desire, whether repeated rejection caused him to withdraw sexually, or whether both have reinforced each other.
Could he have conditioned himself to associate sex with me with rejection, while pornography became his preferred source of sexual gratification? Or am I just not attractive as a person anymore?
I’ve recently had a breakthrough about my own behaviour. I realise I wasn’t simply uninterested in sex. There was unresolved hurt underneath my rejection.
I think we created a vicious cycle:

Unresolved betrayal and insecurity → sexual rejection → his feelings of rejection → withdrawal of sexual desire → pornography becoming a substitute for intimacy → further sexual and emotional distance.
I want to take responsibility for my part in this too.

I actually miss intimacy. We had wonderful sexual chemistry at the beginning of our relationship, and I know I’m a passionate person. I think I’ve suppressed that side of myself for years because it was easier than confronting the complicated emotions surrounding sex. When we have sex, I sometimes remember the bad times and that he may find other women more attractive than me, and I am unable to enjoy it.

MY QUESTIONS 1. Can a man genuinely condition himself to stop desiring his wife after years of repeated sexual rejection? Can this become an almost unconscious response? I always thought that a man will feel automatically elated to want the intimacy back after the wife stops rejecting and initiates. 2. Can that desire return after years of suppression, or can sexual attraction disappear permanently? 3. Can frequent porn use affect a man’s desire for partnered sex, even if he uses it for a quick release? 4. If he can become aroused through porn and masturbation but loses his erection or cannot orgasm during sex with his wife, what could explain this? 5. Have any couples experienced something similar and successfully rebuilt their sexual chemistry? 6. Previously I have nothing against porn as I felt that at least my husband is releasing through a fake screen and not having fantasies about real women. Will quitting porn cold turkey cause him to redirect his sexual desires to real women around him and not for me?

My husband deeply loves me and I feel it and I love him too and I’m happy with the life we’ve built. But I’m prepared to leave and get a divorce if the issue cannot be resolved. I also don’t want to spend the rest of my life in a marriage where we’re wonderful companions but no longer sexually desire each other.
For me, marriage is about more than companionship. I want romance, passion, chemistry and to feel desired by my husband. I want him to experience those things too.

Has anyone been through this? Is it possible to get the sexual spark back? I’d would also appreciate honest perspectives from men who have experienced porn-related sexual difficulties or lost desire for their wives after repeated rejection.
This hurts me deeply. And I am deeply fearful. Thank you so much for your help.

Edit: I appreciate every feedback. I finally recognized my mistake but a little late. I would like to ask a follow up question to men on this thread - What does it mean when he said I’m attractive but he no longer has sexual desire for me as he has conditioned himself to that? Was that a protective mechanism or I’m truly unattractive to him now? Will anything I do bring it back?
Edit 2: He doesn’t want to split, and says he loves me so much that it doesn’t matter even if we don’t have sex. I am so confused.

Edit 3: He sometimes requests me to sit with him and cuddle for a long time and was loving and affectionate, even if there is no sex. I never thought he was ever sexually frustrated as he never show it.

Edit 4: When I was affectionate with him 2 years ago, he started initiating a lot. And I could tell when we had sex, he did it with love and eye contact and deep kissing. And when other times he doesn’t feel appreciated, it was different. So I think there is hope. He loves me, but he doesn’t reveal to me the issues in our marriage, perhaps not to make me feel bad. He said it doesn’t matter as long as I’m happy. But it matters to me. That was what we got to this point.
